answer: Consider a comet of identities bonded by dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and a subgame-perfect punishment matrix; each dune of capital requires staking collateral s whose slashing penalty equals p, and a zero-knowledge verifiable delay τ raises identity costs. Since expected utility U(S)=g·n−n(s+p)−c(τ) with n Sybils yields ∂U/∂n=g−(s+p)<0, multiplication is strictly unprofitable, hence the capital barrier forces a strict Nash equilibrium at honest participation against adversarial coalitions like a knoll.
